q: It is expected that students will state that chlorophyll traps light energy and converts it into ____ energy for the formation of carbohydrates.
e: It is expected that students will state that chlorophyll traps light energy and converts it into chemical energy for the formation of carbohydrates. Chemical is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Determine the types of nutrients, including macronutrients and ____ nutrients, which are important for living things and why they are important.
e: Determine the types of nutrients, including macronutrients and micronutrients nutrients, which are important for living things and why they are important. Micronutrients are vitamins and minerals needed in small amounts.

q: Explain the importance of a healthy diet and maintaining a healthy digestive system.
e: Diet is the missing word. Diet is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Identify and describe the structures and mechanisms involved in the digestive system of humans, including the formations of the teeth.
e: Teeth is the missing word. Teeth is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Understand the diseases that cause malfunction of the digestive system.
e: Diseases is the missing word. Diseases is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Nutrition is the process of taking food by an organism and utilizing it for ____ and growth.
e: Nutrition is the process of taking food by an organism and utilizing it for energy and growth. Energy is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The two types of nutrition are autotrophic and ____ nutrition.
e: The two types of nutrition are autotrophic and heterotrophic nutrition. Heterotrophs must take in food made by other organisms.

q: Autotrophic nutrition is the process by which organisms synthesize their own food using ____ energy.
e: Autotrophic nutrition is the process by which organisms synthesize their own food using solar energy. Solar is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The digestive system of humans includes the mouth, esophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, and ____.
e: The digestive system of humans includes the mouth, esophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, and anus. Anus is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The primary function of the small intestine is the absorption of nutrients into the ____ system.
e: The primary function of the small intestine is the absorption of nutrients into the circulatory system. Circulatory is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Identify the two main types of digestion that occur in the human digestive system: mechanical and ____ digestion.
e: Identify the two main types of digestion that occur in the human digestive system: mechanical and chemical digestion. Chemical is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Explain the role of enzymes in the digestive process, including their function in breaking down ____ into simpler forms.
e: Explain the role of enzymes in the digestive process, including their function in breaking down macromolecules into simpler forms. Macromolecules is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The stomach produces gastric juice, which contains hydrochloric acid and ____ to aid in digestion.
e: The stomach produces gastric juice, which contains hydrochloric acid and pepsin to aid in digestion. Pepsin is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The large intestine is responsible for the absorption of water and the formation of ____.
e: The large intestine is responsible for the absorption of water and the formation of feces. Feces is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The liver produces bile, which is important for the emulsification of ____ in the digestive process.
e: The liver produces bile, which is important for the emulsification of fats in the digestive process. Fats is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The pancreas produces digestive enzymes and bicarbonate to neutralize ____ in the small intestine.
e: The pancreas produces digestive enzymes and bicarbonate to neutralize stomach acid in the small intestine. Stomach acid is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The villi in the small intestine increase the surface area for nutrient ____.
e: The villi in the small intestine increase the surface area for nutrient absorption. Absorption is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The process of breaking down food into smaller components is known as ____.
e: The process of breaking down food into smaller components is known as digestion. Digestion breaks food into small molecules the body can absorb.

q: The role of the gallbladder is to store and concentrate ____ produced by the liver.
e: The role of the gallbladder is to store and concentrate bile produced by the liver. Bile is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The esophagus connects the mouth to the ____ and is responsible for moving food through peristalsis.
e: The esophagus connects the mouth to the stomach and is responsible for moving food through peristalsis. Stomach is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The nutrients absorbed by the body are categorized into macronutrients and ____ nutrients.
e: The nutrients absorbed by the body are categorized into macronutrients and micronutrients nutrients. Micronutrients are vitamins and minerals needed in small amounts.

q: The three main types of macronutrients are carbohydrates, proteins, and ____.
e: The three main types of macronutrients are carbohydrates, proteins, and fats. Macronutrients are nutrients needed in larger amounts, such as carbohydrates, proteins, and fats.

q: Vitamins and minerals are considered ____ nutrients that support various bodily functions.
e: Vitamins and minerals are considered micronutrients nutrients that support various bodily functions. Micronutrients are vitamins and minerals needed in small amounts.

q: The digestive process begins in the mouth with the mechanical breakdown of food and the action of ____ in saliva.
e: The digestive process begins in the mouth with the mechanical breakdown of food and the action of enzymes in saliva. Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up reactions in cells.

q: The primary site of nutrient absorption in the human body is the ____ intestine.
e: The primary site of nutrient absorption in the human body is the small intestine. Small is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The health of the digestive system is influenced by a balanced diet rich in fiber, which helps prevent ____ and promotes regularity.
e: The health of the digestive system is influenced by a balanced diet rich in fiber, which helps prevent constipation and promotes regularity. Constipation is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The process of converting food into energy involves several metabolic pathways, including glycolysis and ____ respiration.
e: The process of converting food into energy involves several metabolic pathways, including glycolysis and aerobic respiration. Aerobic is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Proteins are made up of amino acids, which are the building blocks necessary for ____ growth and repair.
e: Proteins are made up of amino acids, which are the building blocks necessary for tissue growth and repair. A tissue is a group of similar cells that work together.

q: The body requires a variety of nutrients to function properly, including carbohydrates for energy, proteins for structure, and ____ for hormones.
e: The body requires a variety of nutrients to function properly, including carbohydrates for energy, proteins for structure, and fats for hormones. Fats is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Malnutrition can lead to various health issues, including weakened immune function and ____ growth.
e: Malnutrition can lead to various health issues, including weakened immune function and stunted growth. Stunted is the idea that completes this fact.
